title: Research sprint goal: Research: secrets, identities and signed requests for a small self-managed fleet
goal: The sprint goal's open questions are answered from official sources (project docs, RFCs, vendor docs; kb tools first, live docs for the gaps) and written as kb facts and gap entries through the kb skills. Open (pack coverage none, weak or a false good, 2026-10-11): (1) sops with age: .sops.yaml creation_rules, recipients per file, key_groups and shamir_threshold, updatekeys and rotate, and what git history keeps after a rotation; age identities and recipients; (2) Shamir secret sharing of a root identity among K of N holders and maintained tools that split and recombine it; (3) credential ceilings and rotation by minting at the issuer then verifying by use: GitLab token lifetime and rotate API, Cloudflare API token TTL and roll, Discord bot token reset, R2 S3 credentials; (4) BuildKit secret mounts against build args and what image history keeps; (5) Ed25519 request signing over HTTP (RFC 9421: created, expires, nonce, replay windows) and whether an Ed25519 key can be derived from an age X25519 identity; (6) short-lived single-use enrolment tokens (e.g. GitLab runner and Kubernetes bootstrap tokens); (7) Discord OAuth2 with PKCE for a public client (RFC 7636) and OIDC id_token claims and their validation (iss, sub, aud, exp, iat, nonce); (8) UUIDv7 (RFC 9562 layout, monotonicity, Postgres uuidv7()); (9) envelope encryption of Postgres columns with pgcrypto and per-site data keys, and blind indexes (HMAC under a separate key) with their leakage. Already answered: GitLab protected-only CI variables (gitlab/variables.md, gitlab/protected-branches-tags.md), GitLab CI ID token claims (auth/gitlab-ci-identity.md), age and sops lack a rotation hook (auth/key-management-options.md).
